evidence.source_excerpt: One thing you'll notice is that since May of 2022, the Fed's balance sheet has been declining. ... But zooming in on recent history, you can see the Fed is actually expanding their balance sheet. Yet again, balance sheet is going up. That's easing. ... This is the long-term chart of the Federal Funds rate. And you can see that again from 2022 through 2023, the Fed was raising interest rates, and then they kept them steady up until September of 2024. That was a tightening environment. But since 2024, the Fed has been lowering interest rates and recently they voted to keep them steady.
